Lenovo delivers record Q2 performance, confident in long-term Hybrid AI opportunities

HONG KONG--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY), together with its subsidiaries (‘the Group’), today reported second quarter results for fiscal year 2026/27, demonstrating strong growth, a leap forward in profitability, and structural enhancements to the Group’s business fundamentals.

Overall Group revenue for the second quarter reached an all-time high of US$30.2 billion, up 48% year-on-year. All business groups delivered record second-fiscal-quarter revenue while demonstrating strong profitability, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) becoming an engine of hyper-growth with operating profit surpassing US$1 billion for the first time. Adjusted net income[1] was up 166% year-on-year to US$1.4 billion, with adjusted net margin improvements of two percentage points year-on-year. AI-related revenue[2] grew 79% year-on-year, surpassing the US$10 billion mark for the first time and accounting for 36% of total Group revenue in Q2.

Performance was underpinned by broad-based momentum across the Group’s diversified portfolio and balanced growth across all sales geographies. Business fundamentals continued to strengthen as faster growth in higher-value segments reshaped the Group’s profit mix. This diversification helps mitigate industry-wide cost pressures and exposure to device-demand cycles, supporting a more resilient and sustainable profitability profile.

The Group continues to maintain disciplined cash and capital management, balancing strong revenue growth and industry-wide higher component costs with controlled capital expenditure and credit risk controls for large AI infrastructure projects. In this quarter, it generated US$1.6 billion in operating cash flow and US$1.2 billion in free cash flow.

Market Outlook

Lenovo remains highly confident in the long-term growth opportunities across both infrastructure and devices. As AI shifts from training to inferencing, rapidly expanding real-world use cases are driving sustained compute demand across cloud, edge, and enterprise environments. Cloud Service Provider revenue for the Group grew nearly 170% year-on-year, and Enterprise & SMB infrastructure revenue was up 200% year-on-year. At the same time, AI democratization is creating new demand for intelligent, agent-enabled devices as well as new form factors, as more AI data and workloads are generated at the edge. With a full-stack Hybrid AI portfolio spanning devices, edge, infrastructure, solutions and services, Lenovo is uniquely positioned as a full-stack player to capture opportunities and value across the market, as well as extend its leadership.

Lenovo’s Board of Directors declared an interim dividend of 9.0 HK cents per share.

Chairman and CEO quote – Yuanqing Yang:

“Lenovo delivered another exceptional quarter, where we have sustained strong growth, made a leap forward in profitability, and structurally enhanced our business fundamentals, together demonstrating the success of our transformation from a PC leader into a global full-stack compute leader. Now, the real-world AI adoption is booming, which will not only drive sustained growth in infrastructure demand but also unlock tremendous growth potential in the device market. With our Hybrid AI strategy, full-stack portfolio across Client-Edge-Cloud, as well as strong financial discipline and operational resilience, we are confident in sustaining this strong momentum and reaching US$100 billion in annual revenue as early as this fiscal year.”

CFO quote – Winston Cheng:

“Our results this quarter demonstrate the strength of Lenovo’s geographically diverse business and balanced customer mix, while marking further progress toward our long-term net-margin ambitions of more than 5%. This, combined with disciplined working-capital management and controlled capital expenditure, gives us the flexibility to invest in organic growth while maintaining strong liquidity, a resilient balance sheet and our investment-grade credit profile. Together, our operational excellence and financial discipline position Lenovo to capture long-term demand for AI compute and deliver sustainable, profitable growth.”

Q2 results:

Intelligent Devices Group (IDG):

  • Revenue for IDG increased 15% year-on-year to record second fiscal quarter revenue of US$17.4 billion, with double-digit year-on-year revenue growth from PCs and smart devices.
  • IDG’s industry-leading operating margin was well maintained at 7.1%, despite a challenging market environment, reflecting the Group’s operational excellence, supply chain resilience, and continued innovation.
  • Global PC market share leadership was further strengthened, reaching 23.8% and extending Lenovo’s lead over the #2 player to an all-time high of more than seven percentage points.
  • The smartphone business delivered record second-quarter revenue, with double-digit year-on-year growth.

Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG):

  • ISG delivered the strongest quarter in its history in terms of both revenue and profit, with revenue reaching US$11.3 billion, up 178% year-on-year, and operating profit exceeding US$1 billion for the first time. Operating margin expanded to a record 9.6%.
  • ISG strengthened its global market leadership in traditional server, ranking number one in global x86 server shipments for the first time with 16%[3] market share, up six percentage points year-on-year.
  • Enterprise & SMB revenue grew 200% year-on-year. GPU server revenue grew more than 300% year-on-year, supported by a pipeline that grew 48% quarter-on-quarter to US$80 billion.
  • In the first full quarter as part of the Lenovo Group, Infinidat delivered its best quarter ever – with the high-end storage portfolio expanding ISG’s enterprise storage capabilities.

Solutions and Services Group (SSG):

  • SSG delivered record quarterly revenue of US$3.1 billion, up 20% year-on-year, and surpassing US$3 billion for the first time. Operating margin expanded 3.7 percentage points to a record 26%.
  • SSG is growing nearly 2x faster than the broader services market, an outperformance increasingly being driven by higher-value segments as enterprise AI-led offerings accelerate. Managed Services, Projects & Solutions reached a record 63% of SSG revenue, demonstrating the strength of SSG’s tech-led, labor-light model.
  • AI Services continued to deliver triple-digit year-on-year revenue growth, as SSG scaled repeatable AI-powered solutions and Lenovo IP across industries, with momentum in areas including retail, manufacturing and sports.
  • AI Library is also scaling proven, validated use cases across industries and functions, helping customers move from AI experimentation to measurable business outcomes up to 24 times faster.

Corporate highlights

Achievements, announcements, and notable commitments over the past quarter include:

  • Lenovo climbed 43 places to #153 on Fortune’s annual Global 500 List, making it the highest ranking in the company’s history and one of the most significant advances in recent years. The recognition underscores Lenovo’s position as one of the world’s 500 largest companies by revenue.
  • Lenovo received the highest possible rating by Hang Seng Indexes company advancing from its AA+ rating of last year to AAA this year, as well as the highest Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) scores for any company within the technology industry.
  • The Group was named to TIME’s World’s Best Companies 2026 list for the first time, ranking no. 51 globally among leading companies worldwide. The ranking, developed by TIME in partnership with Statista, recognizes top-performing companies around the world based on three primary dimensions: employee satisfaction, revenue growth, and sustainability transparency. Lenovo achieved an overall score of 87.51, with its growth performance categorized as “Very High.”
  • For the third year in a row, Fast Company recognized Lenovo among its annual Best Workplaces for Innovators list. The Group was named as a finalist in both the Best Workplaces for Innovators: AI, Automation and Machine Learning Excellence and Best Workplaces for Innovators: North America categories.
  • Lenovo has been recognized as a World’s Top Disability Inclusive business through the Disability Index, the world’s leading benchmarking tool for measuring and advancing disability inclusion in business.
  • Tech World, Lenovo’s annual global innovation event, will return to CES® 2027 in Las Vegas. Hosted at Sphere and part of the CES Keynote lineup, Tech World will bring together a visionary lineup of speakers and breakthrough innovations with a first-of-its-kind immersive technology and music experience.

[2] Note on AI-related revenue: AI Devices: PCs and Smartphones equipped with NPU; AI Servers: GPU Servers; AI Services: Services that enable customer to build, scale & manage AI.

About Lenovo

Lenovo is a US$83 billion revenue global technology powerhouse, ranked #153 in the Fortune Global 500, and serving millions of customers every day in 180 markets. Guided by its vision of “Smarter Technology for All”, Lenovo is executing a Hybrid AI strategy that spans Personal AI – one personal AI, multiple devices; and Enterprise AI – helping customers turn data into insights and value. This strategy is delivered through the Group’s commitment to world-class innovation and a full-stack AI portfolio, including devices (PCs, workstations, smartphones, tablets, accessories), infrastructure solutions (server, storage, edge, high-performance computing and software defined infrastructure), as well as software, solutions, and services. With a global footprint spanning more than 20 research and development locations and a global supply chain that includes more than 30 manufacturing sites across 11 markets, Lenovo is widely recognized for its operational excellence. Lenovo is listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange under Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY). Learn more at www.lenovo.com and follow the latest news in our newsroom.

  • Poster presented today at CTOS 2026 expands on the survival data first reported in the abstract (announced 11 November 2026), which showed a 12-month disease-free survival (DFS) of 81.1% in patients with resectable soft tissue sarcoma.
  • Patients with post-treatment tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) levels above 310 cells/mm² had 95.0% 12-month DFS compared with 64.9% in patients with lower TIL levels.
  • Patients with treatment-related hyalinisation and fibrosis greater than 52% had 93.8% 12-month DFS compared with 71.4% in patients with lower levels.
  • Results build on previously reported strong pathological responses and further support the potential of efti-based combination therapy.

SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Immutep Limited (ASX: IMM; NASDAQ: IMMP) (“Immutep” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel LAG-3 immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune diseases, today announced new data from the investigator-initiated EFTISARC-NEO Phase II study presented at the Connective Tissue Oncology Society (CTOS) 2026 Annual Meeting (Poster number P 448).

The study is evaluating Immutep’s eftilagimod alfa (efti) in combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) and radiotherapy before surgery in patients with high-risk, resectable soft tissue sarcoma. Forty patients were enrolled, and 38 patients underwent surgery and were included in the survival evaluation.

The latest analysis currently shows a disease-free survival (DFS) of 81.1% at 12 months. The current Kaplan-Meier estimate at 18 months is also 81.1%, although this later time point remains immature, and follow-up is ongoing. Among the 38 patients who underwent surgery and were evaluated, eight patients had experienced disease recurrence at the data cut-off (April 30, 2026).

Table 1 – Survival results for soft tissue sarcoma patients from EFTISARC-NEO

OutcomeLatest Analysis

18-month disease-free survival (immature)81.1%
12-month local recurrence-free survival94.1%

Median follow-up19.1 months


In addition, exploratory analyses showed that higher levels of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) and greater hyalinisation and fibrosis after treatment may be associated with better DFS. In particular, patients with post-treatment TIL levels above 310 cells/mm² had 95.0% 12-month DFS compared with 64.9% in patients with lower TIL levels. Patients with treatment-related hyalinisation and fibrosis greater than 52% had 93.8% 12-month DFS compared with 71.4% in patients with lower levels of hyalinisation and fibrosis. The presence of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and baseline expression of PD-L1, LAG-3 and TIGIT did not correlate with survival outcomes.

These survival and exploratory findings build on previously reported EFTISARC-NEO results in which the trial met its primary endpoint with a median tumour hyalinisation/fibrosis of 51.5% following neoadjuvant therapy with efti, pembrolizumab and radiotherapy. The new data are consistent with efti's mechanism of action, in which activation of antigen-presenting cells drives a stronger anti-tumour T cell response, and suggest that a stronger immune response in the tumour may be associated with improved patient survival outcomes.

Pawel Sobczuk, MD PhD, one of the Principal Investigators of EFTISARC-NEO, said: “These results are highly encouraging for patients with high-risk soft tissue sarcoma, where recurrence remains a major concern despite surgery and radiotherapy. Disease-free survival of approximately 81% maintained through 12 months and on a preliminary basis also at 18 months is an important observation, and the association between a strong immune response in the tumour and better disease-free survival is particularly compelling. Together with the substantial pathological responses previously reported, the findings reinforce the potential of this novel neoadjuvant approach and provide a strong rationale for continued follow-up and further clinical evaluation.”

Marc Voigt, CEO of Immutep, said: “With the data to date, EFTISARC-NEO is delivering an increasingly coherent and encouraging picture. The marked difference in outcomes between patients with higher and lower post-treatment immune cell infiltration is especially notable and is consistent with efti’s potential to help generate a stronger anti-tumour immune response. We believe these results strengthen the rationale for further potential clinical development in this indication, where patients remain in need of more effective treatment options.”

The poster is available on the Posters & Publications page of Immutep’s website.

Next Steps

Immutep anticipates reporting additional data from EFTISARC-NEO in CY2027.

Subject to regulatory interactions, manufacturing timelines, partnering arrangements and available resources, the Company is preparing to advance efti into a registration-directed clinical trial in neoadjuvant soft tissue sarcoma, targeting initiation in H2 CY2027.

About EFTISARC-NEO

EFTISARC-NEO is an investigator-initiated, open-label Phase II trial evaluating eftilagimod alfa (efti) in combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) and radiotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment for patients with resectable soft tissue sarcoma. The trial is led by the Maria Skłodowska-Curie National Research Institute of Oncology in Warsaw, Poland, and is primarily funded by a grant from the Polish Medical Research Agency, with Immutep supplying efti.

The primary endpoint is pathological response, measured as the percentage of tumour hyalinisation/fibrosis at resection. Secondary endpoints include safety, disease-free survival, local recurrence-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, overall survival, radiological response and health-related quality of life. Forty patients were enrolled, with enrolment completed in January 2025 (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06128863).

About Eftilagimod Alfa (efti)

Eftilagimod alfa (efti) is Immutep’s proprietary soluble LAG-3 protein and MHC Class II agonist that activates antigen-presenting cells through the MHC Class II pathway, engaging both innate and adaptive immunity, including the priming of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and the production of co-stimulatory signals and cytokines. Its favourable safety profile enables combination with anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy. Efti has received Fast Track designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in first-line head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and first-line non-small cell lung cancer, and Orphan Drug Designation in soft tissue sarcoma.

About Immutep

Immutep is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune disease. The Company is a pioneer in the understanding and advancement of therapeutics related to Lymphocyte Activation Gene-3 (LAG-3), and its diversified product portfolio harnesses LAG-3’s ability to stimulate or suppress the immune response. Immutep is dedicated to leveraging its expertise to bring innovative treatment options to patients in need and to maximise value for shareholders. For more information, please visit www.immutep.com.

Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially include risks associated with clinical trial outcomes, regulatory developments, and the Company’s ability to advance its product candidates.

CLEVELAND, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyster‑Yale, Inc. (NYSE: HY) today announced the pricing of its offering of $135,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 7.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031 (the "notes") in a private offering to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"). The offering size was increased from the previously announced offering size of $125,000,000 aggregate principal amount of notes. The issuance and sale of the notes is scheduled to close on November 23, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Hyster‑Yale granted the initial purchasers of the notes an option to purchase, for settlement within a period of 13 days from, and including, the date the notes are first issued, up to an additional $20,000,000 aggregate principal amount of notes.

The notes will be general senior unsecured obligations of Hyster‑Yale and will accrue interest at a rate of 7.50% per annum, payable semi-annually in arrears on May 15 and November 15 of each year, beginning on May 15, 2027. The notes will mature on November 15, 2031, unless earlier repurchased, redeemed or converted in accordance with their terms. Before July 15, 2031, noteholders will have the right to convert their notes only upon the occurrence of certain events. At any time from, and including, July 15, 2031, noteholders may convert their notes at their election until the close of business on the second scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date, irrespective of these conditions. Hyster‑Yale will settle conversions by paying cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted and paying or delivering, as applicable, cash, shares of its Class A common stock (the "Class A common stock") or a combination of cash and shares of Class A common stock, at Hyster‑Yale's election, in respect of the remainder, if any, of its conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted. The initial conversion rate is 55.1207 shares of Class A common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes, which represents an initial conversion price of approximately $18.14 per share of Class A common stock. The initial conversion price represents a premium of approximately 17.5% over the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on November 18, 2026, which was $15.44 per share. The conversion rate will be subject to adjustment upon the occurrence of certain events, but will not be adjusted for any accrued and unpaid interest.

Hyster‑Yale may not redeem the notes prior to November 20, 2029, except in the event of a cleanup redemption (as defined below). The notes will be redeemable, in whole or in part (subject to certain limitations, including a partial redemption limitation), for cash at Hyster‑Yale's option at any time, and from time to time, on a redemption date on or after November 20, 2029 and before the 61st scheduled trading day immediately prior to the maturity date, if the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock has been at least 130% of the conversion price then in effect for a specified period of time and if certain other conditions are satisfied. The redemption price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the relevant redemption date.

In addition, Hyster‑Yale may redeem for cash all, but not less than all, of the notes at any time before the 61st scheduled trading day immediately prior to the maturity date if the aggregate principal amount of the notes that remains outstanding at such time is less than 10% of the aggregate principal amount of the notes initially issued under the indenture and certain other conditions are satisfied (a "cleanup redemption"). The redemption price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the relevant redemption date.

If certain corporate events that constitute a "fundamental change" (as defined in the indenture that will govern the notes) occur, then, subject to certain conditions and exceptions, noteholders may require Hyster‑Yale to repurchase their notes for cash. The fundamental change repurchase price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the applicable fundamental change repurchase date.

Hyster‑Yale estimates that the net proceeds from the offering will be approximately $129.7 million (or approximately $149.1 million if the initial purchasers fully exercise their option to purchase additional notes), after deducting the initial purchasers' discounts and commissions and Hyster‑Yale's estimated offering expenses. Hyster‑Yale intends to use the net proceeds from the offering of the notes, together with cash on hand, (i) to repay $110.0 million of the $213.2 million principal amount outstanding under the term loan under its Amended and Restated Term Loan Credit Agreement, dated as of May 28, 2021 (the "2021 Credit Agreement"), (ii) to pay the approximately $13.5 million cost of the capped call transactions (as described below), (iii) to repurchase approximately $15 million of shares of Class A common stock concurrently with the pricing of the notes (as described below), and (iv) for general corporate purposes. If the initial purchasers exercise their option to purchase additional notes, Hyster‑Yale expects to use a portion of the net proceeds from the sale of the additional notes to enter into additional capped call transactions with the option counterparties, to repay additional principal amounts outstanding under the term loan under its 2021 Credit Agreement and, to the extent any proceeds remain, for general corporate purposes. The Company intends to repay the remaining principal amount outstanding under the term loan under its 2021 Credit Agreement on or prior to its maturity with additional long-term debt that is on terms acceptable to the Company.

Hyster‑Yale expects to use approximately $15 million of the net proceeds from the offering to repurchase approximately 971,000 shares of Class A common stock in privately negotiated transactions effected with or through one of the initial purchasers or its affiliate concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the notes (the "concurrent share repurchase"). The purchase price per share in the concurrent share repurchase will be $15.44 per share, which is the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on the date of the pricing of the notes. The concurrent share repurchase could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of Class A common stock, including concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the notes, and could have resulted in a higher effective conversion price for the notes. Hyster‑Yale cannot predict the magnitude of such market activity or the overall effect it will have on the price of the notes or the Class A common stock and the corresponding effect on the initial conversion price of the notes.

In connection with the pricing of the notes, Hyster‑Yale entered into privately negotiated capped call transactions with certain of the initial purchasers and their affiliates and certain other financial institutions (the "option counterparties"). The capped call transactions cover, subject to customary adjustments substantially similar to those applicable to the notes, the number of shares of Class A common stock initially underlying the notes. The capped call transactions are generally expected to reduce the potential dilution to the Class A common stock upon any conversion of the notes and/or offset any potential cash payments Hyster‑Yale is required to make in excess of the principal amount of such converted notes, as the case may be, with such reduction and/or offset subject to a cap based on the cap price. The cap price of the capped call transactions is initially $27.02 per share, which represents a premium of 75% over the last reported sale price per share of the Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on November 18, 2026 (which was $15.44 per share), and is subject to certain adjustments under the terms of the capped call transactions. If the initial purchasers exercise their option to purchase additional notes, then Hyster‑Yale expects to enter into additional capped call transactions with the option counterparties.

Hyster‑Yale has been advised that, in connection with establishing their initial hedges of the capped call transactions, the option counterparties or their respective affiliates expect to enter into various derivative transactions with respect to the Class A common stock and/or purchase shares of Class A common stock concurrently with, or shortly after, the pricing of the notes. This activity could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of the Class A common stock or the notes at that time.

In addition, Hyster-Yale has been advised that the option counterparties or their respective affiliates may modify their hedge positions by entering into or unwinding various derivatives with respect to the Class A common stock and/or purchasing or selling the Class A common stock or other securities of Hyster‑Yale in secondary market transactions following the pricing of the notes and prior to the maturity of the notes (and are likely to do so during any observation period related to a conversion of the notes, following any redemption of the notes or any repurchase of the notes upon a fundamental change, or, to the extent Hyster‑Yale exercises the relevant election under the capped call transactions, following any other repurchase of the notes). This activity could also cause or avoid an increase or a decrease in the market price of the Class A common stock or the notes, which could affect the ability of noteholders to convert the notes and, to the extent the activity occurs during any observation period related to a conversion of the notes, it could affect the number of shares of Class A common stock, if any, and value of the consideration that noteholders will receive upon conversion of the notes.

The notes are being offered only to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act. The offer and sale of the notes and any shares of Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of the notes have not been, and will not be, registered under the Securities Act or any other securities laws, and the notes and any such shares cannot be offered or sold except pursuant to an exemption from, or in a transaction not subject to, the registration requirements of the Securities Act and any other applicable securities laws. This press release does not constitute an offer to sell, or the solicitation of an offer to buy, the notes or any shares of Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of the notes, nor will there be any sale of the notes or any such shares, in any state or other jurisdiction in which such offer, sale or solicitation would be unlawful. This press release does not constitute an offer to buy any shares of Class A common stock in the contemplated repurchase.

SINGAPORE, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- JOYY Inc. (NASDAQ: JOYY) (“JOYY” or the “Company”), a global technology company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights1

  • Net revenues were US$624.6 million, an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • Social Entertainment net revenues increased by 8.8% to US$441.0 million from US$405.5 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • BIGO Ads net revenues increased by 39.6% to US$145.7 million from US$104.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • Shopline net revenues increased by 24.7% to US$37.8 million from US$30.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Operating income was US$13.5 million, compared with US$19.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$13.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Non-GAAP EBITDA2 was US$55.7 million, an increase of 10.1% from US$50.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and compared with US$56.9 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest of JOYY3 was US$59.6 million, compared with US$62.0 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$51.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Non-GAAP net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest and common shareholders of JOYY4 was US$67.1 million, compared with US$72.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$63.5 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Net Cash5 as of September 30, 2026 was US$2,940.5 million.
  • Net Cash from operating activities was US$102.2 million, compared with US$73.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights

Global community:

  • Global average mobile MAUs6 reached 278.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, up by 4.7% from 266.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and up by 0.6% from 277.1 million in the second quarter of 2026. The Company continued to optimize its marketing strategies to focus on return on investment (ROI) and high-value users.

Social Entertainment:

  • In the third quarter, Social Entertainment revenues increased by 8.8% year over year to US$441.0 million, with live streaming revenues reaching US$419.8 million, an 8.1% increase from the corresponding period of 2025. By region, live streaming revenues showed year-over-year growth across all four geographical areas.
  • In the third quarter, core live streaming paying users7 increased by 8.1% year over year to 1.64 million, while ARPPU8 was US$218.7.
  • Bigo Live continued to make enhancements across content operations, streamer ecosystem, and AI-driven capabilities. In content operations, the Company refined its cross-regional content algorithms, expanded live translation coverage and noise-resilient speech recognition, enabling users to discover diverse content and interact with streamers across regions. Improved onboarding and guidance for newly signed streamers contributed to a 4.7-percentage-point sequential increase in the share of newly signed streamers completing their first livestream. The Company also continued to expand AI-generated interactive content and virtual gifts. In September 2026, AI-generated interactive virtual gifts accounted for 35.4% of total virtual gift consumption on Bigo Live.

B2B Initiatives: Advertising Technology and Smart Commerce

  • Beginning in 2022, the Company ramped up efforts to diversify its revenue streams, cultivating its new initiatives in advertising technology and smart commerce. The Company has made steady progress advancing towards its strategic positioning as a global tech company powered by multiple growth engines. In the third quarter, total non-live streaming revenues reached US$204.7 million, up by 34.9% year over year, representing 32.8% of total net revenues of the Company, compared with 28.1% in the corresponding period of 2025.

BIGO Ads:

  • BIGO Ads is a global AI-powered programmatic advertising platform. Launched to provide one-stop marketing and monetization solutions, it leverages deep learning, real-time bidding, and smart bidding models to enable brands to scale user acquisition and app developers to effectively unlock monetization potential through connecting premium global demand.
  • In the third quarter, BIGO Ads’ total revenues grew by 39.6% year over year to US$145.7 million. In particular, BIGO Audience Network, which includes third-party advertising revenues generated on network partners’ traffic properties, maintained robust growth, with revenues increasing by 52.3% year over year.
  • BIGO Ads has access to a vast traffic pool, comprising the Company’s own global average mobile MAU base and an extensive network of third-party traffic through seamless integration of developer traffic across major channels. During the third quarter, Software Development Kit (SDK) traffic scale continued to expand, increasing by 55.6% year over year.
  • Broader traffic coverage, multi-vertical advertiser expansion, and ongoing algorithm optimization continued to fuel growth. Web-based demand grew approximately 328% year over year and 30% quarter over quarter, alongside solid performance from in-app demand.
  • BIGO Ads continued to invest in its algorithm and engineering infrastructure during the quarter. As its cross-channel attribution systems improved and advertiser conversion data accumulated, BIGO Ads broadened its data inputs for model training, improving predictions of conversion probability and user lifetime value. The platform also upgraded its model architecture to support different conversion objectives and traffic types, while refining its bidding algorithm to better assess the value of each ad impression and allocate advertiser budgets more effectively.

Shopline:

  • Shopline serves as a global AI-powered operating system for modern retail. Beyond storefront creation, Shopline offers a deeply integrated suite of merchant services across payments, logistics, marketing, and data analytics. It is an open, extensible omnichannel platform that enables merchants to manage the full commerce value chain from store setup and transactions to fulfillment, customer acquisition, and lifecycle engagement. Shopline has helped merchants in diverse industries across multiple markets to launch and scale their businesses.
  • Shopline currently generates revenues from recurring software subscription fees and a suite of transaction-based value-added services, including localized payment processing (Shopline Payments) and marketing solutions.
  • In the third quarter, Shopline generated revenues of US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year and 10.0% quarter over quarter. Notably, cross-border merchants revenue increased by 77.8% year over year. The Company continued to enhance Shopline Payments with more local payment options, stronger multi-currency payment support, and improved transaction management, helping merchants manage cross-border payments more easily and efficiently.
  • As AI platforms and agents emerge as new channels for product discovery and purchasing, Shopline continued to strengthen its AI Commerce capabilities. On the ecosystem front, Shopline expanded its integrations with leading AI platforms and AI agents, and enhanced its AI tools and interfaces for developers. On the merchant operations front, the Company rolled out its AI-powered commerce assistant, Shopline Omi, spanning product management, customer segmentation, promotional events, multilingual support, and detailed store performance analysis.

Ms. Ting Li, Chairperson and Chief Executive Officer of JOYY, commented, “This quarter, we made further progress toward becoming a global technology company powered by multiple growth engines. Total net revenues reached US$624.6 million, up 15.6% year over year and 5.7% quarter over quarter. Our Social Entertainment business remained on a steady course, while BIGO Ads and Shopline sustained robust performances, driving solid topline expansion and strong operating cash flow generation. We remain steadfast in our commitment to shareholder returns, having returned a total of US$536.0 million year-to-date through November 13, 2026, comprising US$216.2 million in dividends and US$319.8 million in share repurchases.

Social Entertainment revenues grew 8.8% year over year to US$441.0 million, supported by continued enhancements to Bigo Live’s content operations, streamer ecosystem, and AI-driven capabilities. Live streaming revenues and core live streaming paying users both increased 8.1% year over year. BIGO Ads revenues rose 39.6% year over year to US$145.7 million, led by 52.3% year-over-year growth in BIGO Audience Network as we expanded our traffic network, diversified advertiser demand, and improved our algorithms and ad delivery. Shopline revenues reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year, supported by continued expansion among cross-border merchants and strong momentum in Shopline Payments. We also advanced our AI Commerce initiatives to help merchants reach customers through emerging AI-powered shopping channels and strengthen Shopline’s role as an omnichannel e-commerce infrastructure platform.

Looking ahead to 2027, we believe JOYY will enter a pivotal phase in which our established strategy translates into stronger operating results. With clearer strategic trajectories across our three businesses, we are well positioned to deliver diversified and sustainable growth while creating long-term shareholder value.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

NET REVENUES

Net revenues were US$624.6 million, representing an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Social Entertainment net revenues increased by 8.8% to US$441.0 million from US$405.5 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by higher live streaming revenues, as expanded content categories and enhanced localized operations contributed to stronger user engagement and paying conversion across key markets.

BIGO Ads net revenues increased by 39.6% to US$145.7 million from US$104.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by expansion of traffic, elevated advertiser demand across regions and verticals, and enhanced algorithm performance that resulted in improved advertisement delivery efficiency and higher advertiser spending.

Shopline net revenues increased by 24.7% to US$37.8 million from US$30.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by continued merchant adoption and deeper penetration of value-added services.

COST OF REVENUES AND GROSS PROFIT

Cost of revenues was US$407.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$347.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$389.2 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Social Entertainment’s cost of revenues increased by 7.4% year over year to US$274.3 million, and by 3.7% from US$264.6 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher revenue-sharing fees and content costs of US$28.4 million and US$7.9 million, respectively.

BIGO Ads’ cost of revenues increased by 47.9% year over year to US$112.2 million, and by 5.6% from US$106.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher traffic acquisition costs paid to third-party partners in relation to the expansion of BIGO Audience Network.

Shopline’s cost of revenues increased by 30.8% year over year to US$20.9 million, and by 13.9% from US$18.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher payment processing costs, reflecting an increased contribution from payment services to Shopline’s revenue mix.

Gross profit was US$217.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$193.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$201.6 million in the second quarter of 2026. Gross margin was 34.8% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 35.8% in the corresponding period of 2025 and 34.1% in the second quarter of 2026.

OPERATING EXPENSES AND INCOME

Operating expenses were US$204.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$174.2 million in the same period of 2025 and US$188.2 million in the second quarter of 2026. Among the operating expenses, sales and marketing expenses were US$86.7 million, compared with US$72.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$79.6 million in the second quarter of 2026. Research and development expenses were US$59.0 million, compared with US$63.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$53.0 million in the second quarter of 2026. General and administrative expenses were US$58.4 million, compared with US$39.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$55.6 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Operating income was US$13.5 million, compared with US$19.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$13.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Non-GAAP operating income9 was US$46.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$40.7 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$49.1 million in the second quarter of 2026. Non-GAAP operating income margin10 was 7.5% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 7.5% in the corresponding period of 2025 and 8.3% in the second quarter of 2026.

Non-GAAP EBITDA was US$55.7 million, compared with US$50.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$56.9 million in the second quarter of 2026. Non-GAAP EBITDA margin11 was 8.9%, compared with 9.4% in the corresponding period of 2025 and 9.6% in the second quarter of 2026.

NET INCOME

Net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest of JOYY was US$59.6 million, compared with US$62.0 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$51.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. Net income margin was 9.5% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 11.5% in the corresponding period of 2025 and 8.8% in the second quarter of 2026.

Non-GAAP net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest and common shareholders of JOYY was US$67.1 million, compared with US$72.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$63.5 million in the second quarter of 2026. Non-GAAP net income margin12 was 10.7% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 13.4% in the corresponding period of 2025 and 10.7% in the second quarter of 2026.

NET INCOME PER ADS

Diluted net income from continuing operations per ADS13 was US$1.20 in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$1.15 in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$1.01 in the second quarter of 2026.

Non-GAAP diluted net income from continuing operations per ADS14 was US$1.36 in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$1.36 in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$1.24 in the second quarter of 2026.

BALANCE SHEET AND CASH FLOWS

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had net cash of US$2,940.5 million, compared with US$3,258.0 million as of December 31, 2025. For the third quarter of 2026, net cash from operating activities was US$102.2 million.

SHARES OUTSTANDING

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had a total of 952.0 million common shares outstanding, representing the equivalent of 47.6 million ADSs assuming the conversion of all common shares into ADSs.

Business Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company expects net revenues to be between US$650 million and US$669 million. This forecast reflects the Company’s current and preliminary views on the market, operational conditions, and business strategies, which are subject to change, particularly as to the potential impact from macroeconomic uncertainties.

Share Repurchase Programs

Pursuant to the Company’s up-to-US$600 million share repurchase program authorized in May 2026, or the 2026 Share Repurchase Program, which is effective through the end of 2028, the Company had repurchased approximately 1.6 million ADSs for an aggregate consideration of US$120.5 million on the open market during the third quarter of 2026.

Between October 1, 2026 and November 13, 2026, the Company repurchased an additional approximately 0.5 million ADSs, for an aggregate consideration of US$38.4 million under the 2026 Share Repurchase Program. The remaining unutilized amount under the 2026 Share Repurchase Program was approximately US$368.2 million as of November 13, 2026.

Quarterly Dividend Program

On May 22, 2026, the board of directors of the Company authorized a quarterly dividend program, or the 2026 Dividend Program, under which a total of approximately US$900 million in cash will be distributed on a quarterly basis between 2026 and 2028.

Pursuant to the 2026 Dividend Program, the board of directors has accordingly declared a dividend of US$1.59 per ADS, or US$0.0795 per common share, for the third quarter of 2026, which is expected to be paid on January 15, 2027 to shareholders of record as of the close of business on December 30, 2026. The ex-dividend date will be December 30, 2026.

TORRANCE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Emmaus Life Sciences, Inc. (OTCQB: EMMA), a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company and leader in the treatment of sickle cell disease, today reported on its financial condition and results of operations as of and for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights

“Our global net revenues declined for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025 primarily driven by a 44% decrease in U.S. net revenues as our licensing agreement with NeoImmuneTech Inc. (NIT), became effective on May 15, 2026,” commented Willis Lee, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Emmaus. “The decline was partially offset by a related reduction in our operating expenses. Management believes that the conflict in the Middle East also adversely affected net revenues in the region,” he added.

Financial and Operating Results

Net Revenues. Net revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $1.9 million, compared to $3.4 million in the same period in 2025 driven by lower direct sales of Endari® following the company’s execution of the License Agreement with NIT.

Operating Expenses. Total operating expenses for the three months were $1.9 million compared to $2.4 million in the comparable period in 2025. The decrease was due primarily to decreased expenses attributable to the transfer of our sales force to NIT in connection with the license arrangement.

Income (Loss) From Operations. Loss from operations for the three months was $0.4 million compared to income from operations of $0.7 million in the same period in 2025. The changes were due to the decrease in net revenues, partially offset by lower operating expenses.

Other Expense. The company realized other expense of $4.4 million for the three months compared to $2.2 million in the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily due to change in fair value of conversion features derivative based upon an increase in the company’s stock price.

Net Loss. For the three months, the company realized a net loss of $4.7 million, or $0.07 basic loss per share based on approximately 70.2 million weighted-average common shares, compared to net loss of $2.1 million, or $0.03 basic loss per share based on approximately 63.9 million weighted-average common shares in the comparable period in 2025. The increase in net loss was attributable primarily to the decrease in net revenues and increase in other expense.

Liquidity and Capital Resources. At September 30, 2026, the company had cash and cash equivalents of $1.0 million, compared to $2.1 million at December 31, 2025.

About Emmaus Life Sciences

Emmaus Life Sciences, Inc. is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company and leader in the treatment of sickle cell disease. Endari® (L-glutamine oral powder), indicated to reduce the acute complications of sickle cell disease in adults and children 5 years and older, is approved for marketing in the United States, Israel, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Oman and is available on a named patient or early access basis in France, the Netherlands, and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where Emmaus’ application for marketing authorization is awaiting final action by the Saudi Food & Drug Authority. For more information, please visit www.emmausmedical.com.

About Endari® (prescription grade L-glutamine oral powder)

Endari®, Emmaus’ prescription grade L-glutamine oral powder, was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in July 2017 for treating sickle cell disease in adult and pediatric patients five years of age and older.

Indication

Endari® is indicated to reduce the acute complications of sickle cell disease in adult and pediatric patients five years of age and older.

Important Safety Information

The most common adverse reactions (incidence >10 percent) in clinical studies were constipation, nausea, headache, abdominal pain, cough, pain in extremities, back pain, and chest pain.

Adverse reactions leading to treatment discontinuation included one case each of hypersplenism, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, burning sensation, and hot flash.

The safety and efficacy of Endari® in pediatric patients with sickle cell disease younger than five years of age has not been established.

For more information, please see full Prescribing Information of Endari® at: www.ENDARIrx.com/PI.

About Sickle Cell Disease

There are approximately 100,000 people living with sickle cell disease (SCD) in the United States and millions more globally. The sickle gene is found in every ethnic group, not just among those of African descent; and in the United States an estimated 1-in-365 African Americans and 1-in-16,300 Hispanic Americans are born with SCD.1 The genetic mutation responsible for SCD causes an individual's red blood cells to distort into a "C" or a sickle shape, reducing their ability to transport oxygen throughout the body. These sickled red blood cells break down rapidly, become very sticky, and develop a propensity to clump together, which causes them to become stuck and cause damage within blood vessels. The result is reduced blood flow to distal organs, which leads to physical symptoms of incapacitating pain, tissue and organ damage, and early death.2

JLL is recognized for transforming facility management through an integrated Workplace Management platform, digital innovation, and sector-focused execution that strengthens operational resilience and business performance.

SAN ANTONIO, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As facility management continues to evolve from a largely operational function into a strategic contributor to workplace performance and enterprise resilience, JLL is demonstrating how an integrated approach can create measurable value for organizations across complex environments. Frost & Sullivan recognizes JLL with the 2026 North American Competitive Strategy Leadership Recognition in Facility Management for its ability to combine strategic transformation, digital capabilities, and sector expertise to strengthen its competitive position and deliver integrated facility management (IFM) solutions across the region.

Frost & Sullivan evaluates companies through a rigorous benchmarking process across two core dimensions: strategy effectiveness and strategy execution. JLL excelled in both, demonstrating its ability to align strategic initiatives with evolving market demands while executing them with consistency, scale, and measurable impact. "JLL is a recognized leader in IFM and workplace solutions across North America. Its competitive position is built on a clear strategic progression: redefining Facility Management through the Workplace Management platform, aligning its operating structure to support integrated delivery, and scaling digital and sector-specific capabilities across the United States and Canada. This approach enables JLL to serve commercial office, financial services, life sciences, technology, industrial and advanced manufacturing, data centers, healthcare, and government clients while linking facility operations more directly to business performance," said Janice Wung, Industry Principal, Homes & Buildings, Frost & Sullivan.

JLL's strategic approach centers on its Workplace Management platform, which brings together facilities management, technical services, sustainable operations, safety, sourcing and procurement, workplace experience, and technology-enabled delivery under a single operating structure. The platform supports greater standardization, governance, and scalability across multi-site portfolios while maintaining flexibility for sector-specific requirements.

Digital innovation further differentiates JLL's approach to facility management. Technologies, including Corrigo, JLL Smart Building Platform, Azara, and JLL Falcon AI, support work order and asset management, predictive maintenance, energy optimization, workplace analytics, and portfolio-level performance visibility. These capabilities enable clients to move beyond reactive facility operations toward more proactive, data-driven decision-making.

"We are honored Frost & Sullivan is recognizing JLL's work in facilities management," said Chris Fernandez, Americas Head of Workplace Management at JLL. "At its core, facilities management is about creating environments where people can do their best work while ensuring the buildings they depend on operate safely, reliably and efficiently every day. FM has evolved far beyond maintaining physical assets. Today, it sits at the intersection of workplace experience, operational resilience and business performance. This award reflects the dedication of our teams across North America who help clients care for both their buildings and the people inside them, ensuring workplaces support productivity, collaboration and long-term success."

Frost & Sullivan's recognition comes while broader changes are underway across the facility management industry. JLL's recent Global State of Facilities Management Report 2026 reveals that half of occupiers already view FM as a significant source of competitive advantage, with that figure projected to rise to more than four in five organizations by 2030. Meanwhile, 45% of occupiers are scaling AI across FM operations while nearly 70% have experienced disruptions from skilled labor shortages and technical skills gaps. These converging trends are accelerating demand for integrated workplace management strategies that combine operational expertise, technology and workforce capabilities to support business performance and resilience.

JLL has also demonstrated its ability to translate strategy into execution across complex, high-value environments. In 2025, the company secured integrated facilities management for WestJet's 1.9 million-square-foot portfolio spanning its headquarters and 17 Canadian airport locations, along with the facility maintenance and operations mandate for the $9.5 billion JFK New Terminal One project. For a global tech manufacturer, JLL moved the company's U.S. portfolio from reactive repairs to proactive IFM, saving nearly $1 million on HVAC costs in its first eight months and achieving 4% overall savings in the first year. JLL has also partnered with a Fortune 100 semiconductor company to build a digital FM strategy aimed at cost savings and operational excellence. Together, these engagements show JLL's ability to scale integrated facility management across demanding environments where reliability, compliance, operational resilience, and risk management are critical.

The company's competitive position is further strengthened by integrating energy management, decarbonization initiatives, ESG reporting, workplace experience, and space-utilization analysis into its FM delivery model, JLL addresses the increasingly interconnected priorities of corporate real estate, sustainability, HR, and business leaders.

Frost & Sullivan commends JLL for establishing a differentiated approach to facility management that connects operational performance with broader business outcomes. Through its combination of proprietary technology, advisory-led delivery, sector expertise, and customer-focused execution, JLL is helping shape the future of FM across North America.

Each year, Frost & Sullivan presents the Competitive Strategy Leadership recognition to a company that demonstrates outstanding strategy development and implementation, resulting in measurable improvements in market share, customer satisfaction, and competitive positioning. The recognition highlights forward-thinking organizations that are reshaping their industries through innovation and growth excellence.

Frost & Sullivan Best Practices Recognition

Frost & Sullivan's Best Practices Recognitions honor companies across regional and global markets that exhibit exceptional achievement and consistent excellence in areas such as leadership, technological innovation, customer experience, and strategic product development. Each recognition is the result of a rigorous analytical process in which Frost & Sullivan industry experts benchmark performance through comprehensive interviews, deep-dive analysis, and extensive secondary research. The goal is to identify true best-in-class organizations that are driving transformative growth and setting new industry standards.

  • Initial focus on graphene enhanced carbon fibre prepreg, with plans to expand into thermoplastics, resin concentrates, coatings and elastomers.
  • Agreement combines First Graphene's formulation and dispersion expertise with UNITEX's manufacturing and innovation capabilities, and established international supply network.
  • Provides First Graphene with a pathway into China's composites manufacturing and innovation sector and access to wider international markets, helping to accelerate the development, scale-up and global commercialisation of graphene-enhanced materials across a broad range of applications.

Sydney, Australia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - First Graphene Limited (ASX: FGR) (FSE: M11) (OTCQB: FGPHF) ("First Graphene" or "the Company") is pleased to announce it has entered into a Joint Development and Commercialisation Agreement ("the Agreement") with UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd. ("UNITEX"), establishing a strategic collaboration to develop and commercialise graphene enhanced carbon fibre composites and other advanced materials.

The Agreement represents a further step in First Graphene's strategy to commercialise its graphene technologies through strategic development and manufacturing partnerships. The collaboration draws on UNITEX's material development, engineering and manufacturing capabilities in China, providing First Graphene with a pathway into China's significant composites manufacturing sector and the international markets it supplies.

Headquartered in Ningbo, China's Zhejiang province, UNITEX is a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications. Built on its manufacturing capabilities in China, the group combines material development, application engineering and industrial supply chain integration to translate material technologies into commercially viable products and solutions.

With an established customer network spanning more than 100 countries, UNITEX serves industries including automotive, aerospace, semiconductors, energy, marine, construction and sporting goods.

Its capabilities extend from customised material development and engineering support to industrial-scale manufacturing and global supply, providing a foundation for the international commercialisation of jointly developed materials.

The collaboration will combine First Graphene's expertise in graphene selection, formulation and dispersion with UNITEX's materials engineering, manufacturing infrastructure and established supply chain capabilities.

Development and commercialisation program

The initial development program will focus on graphene enhanced carbon fibre prepreg, building on First Graphene's internal research and development activities, which demonstrated improvements in strength and barrier properties through incorporation of graphene into carbon fibre composites.

Where the results justify further development, the parties intend to progress successful formulations through customer validation, manufacturing scale-up and commercialisation, subject to the agreement of applicable commercial terms. The Agreement term is for three years and is cancellable by either party with three months notice.

Beyond carbon fibre prepreg, the collaboration is expected to explore opportunities across thermoplastics, resin concentrates, coatings, elastomers and other advanced materials, broadening the potential applications and commercial reach of First Graphene's graphene technologies.

The Agreement provides First Graphene with an opportunity to leverage UNITEX's material development, engineering and manufacturing capabilities, together with its established international customer network, to accelerate the development and industrialisation of graphene enhanced materials and bring commercially viable products to global markets.

First Graphene Managing Director and CEO, Michael Bell, said:

"Carbon fibre and advanced composites represent an increasingly important growth opportunity for First Graphene, as manufacturers seek innovative ways to improve material performance and deliver greater value to customers.

Our internal development work has demonstrated the potential of graphene to enhance the strength and barrier properties of carbon fibre composites. The next step is translating technical advances into commercially scalable products through partnerships with established manufacturers.

UNITEX brings extensive expertise in materials development, engineering and manufacturing, alongside an established international customer network. This collaboration provides FGR with a strategic pathway into China's composites manufacturing sector and expand its commercial reach across global markets.

Importantly, the opportunity extends well beyond carbon fibre. By combining our respective technical and manufacturing capabilities, we see significant potential to develop graphene-enhanced thermoplastics, coatings and other advanced materials across industrial applications.

This agreement is another important step in our strategy to move graphene innovation from development into commercial markets and expand First Graphene's international presence."

UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd., established in 2017 and headquartered in Ningbo, China, is part of UNITEX Group, a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications. Built on its manufacturing capabilities in China and the integration of China's comprehensive industrial supply chain, UNITEX brings together material development, application engineering and industrialisation to deliver customised solutions for global customers. The group serves customers in more than 100 countries, supporting a broad range of industries from material development through to commercial production and international supply.

SINGAPORE, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- JOYY Inc. (NASDAQ: JOYY) ("JOYY" or the "Company"), a leading global technology company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

In the third quarter, JOYY maintained solid growth momentum. Total revenues reached US$624.6 million, up 15.6% year over year and 5.7% quarter over quarter. Social entertainment revenue was US$441.0 million, up 8.8% year over year. BIGO Ads, including both first-party and third-party businesses, generated US$145.7 million in revenue, up 39.6% year over year, with its third-party advertising business sustaining strong growth of 52.3% year over year. SHOPLINE revenue reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year. The contribution from non-livestreaming revenue further increased to 32.8% of total revenues this quarter, driven by the Company's multi-engine growth strategy.

JOYY's non-GAAP operating income reached US$46.6 million, up 14.6% year over year. Non-GAAP EBITDA reached US$55.7 million, up 10.1% year over year. Operating cash inflow for the quarter was US$102.2 million. As of September 30, 2026, JOYY held US$2.94 billion in net cash. Supported by the Company's strong cash flow generation and solid financial position, it continued to return capital to its shareholders for their long-term support through cash dividends and share repurchases. As of November 13, the Company has returned a total of US$536.0 million to shareholders this year.

Ms. Ting Li, Chairperson and Chief Executive Officer of JOYY, commented, "We have continued to execute our multi-engine growth strategy, strengthening our core Social Entertainment business while developing Ad Tech and Smart Commerce as two new growth engines. Following our investments and business model validation over the past few years, the results of this strategy are becoming increasingly evident in sustained topline expansion. Looking ahead to 2027, we believe JOYY will enter an important phase as we advance our multi-engine growth strategy and translate our progress into stronger operating results. With increasingly clear growth paths across our three businesses, we are confident in the Company's ability to sustain solid revenue growth in 2027. We also expect greater scale, a stronger earnings mix, and improved operating efficiency to drive further growth in operating profitability." 

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Net revenues in the third quarter of 2026 were US$624.6 million, representing an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    - Social Entertainment revenue was US$441.0 million, representing an increase of 8.8% from US$405.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    - BIGO Ads revenue was US$145.7 million, representing an increase of 39.6% from US$104.4 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    - SHOPLINE revenue was US$37.8 million, representing an increase of 24.7% from US$30.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Operating income was US$13.5 million.
  • Non-GAAP1 operating income was US$46.6 million, representing an increase of 14.6% from US$40.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Non-GAAP1 EBITDA was US$55.7 million, representing an increase of 10.1% from US$50.6 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net cash as of September 30, 2026 was US$2940.5 million.
  • Net cash from operating activities was US$102.2 million.

Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights

Social Entertainment Business

In the third quarter, Social Entertainment continued to deliver steady growth, with year-over-year growth momentum further accelerating. The Company's global average mobile MAUs reached 278.8 million, up 4.7% year over year. Livestreaming revenue reached US$419.8 million, up 8.1% year over year and 4.3% quarter over quarter. Driven by effective and refined operations, the number of core livestreaming paying users grew 8.1% year over year and 4.8% quarter over quarter.

Bigo Live, the Company's flagship product, continued its steady revenue growth, supported by ongoing improvements in content operations, its streamer ecosystem, and AI applications. In content operations, Bigo Live continued to build on its strengths as a global social platform to better cater to users' cross-regional content consumption and social interaction needs. Bigo Live further refined its cross-regional content distribution algorithms, expanded live translation coverage, and enhanced speech recognition in complex acoustic environments, making it easier for cross-language communication. These improvements drove continued growth in cross-regional gifting among users in developed markets. In terms of the streamer ecosystem, Bigo Live continued to invest in its community by refining growth and incentive mechanisms for new streamers. In particular, Bigo Live improved onboarding and guidance to help newly signed streamers successfully launch their first livestreams. These efforts contributed to a 4.7-percentage-point increase in the share of newly signed streamers completing their first livestream compared with the previous quarter, bolstering Bigo Live's high-quality content pipeline. Bigo Live continued to integrate AI into livestream interactions and virtual gifting, expanding its AI-generated interactive content and virtual gifts to create a more personalized experience for users. In September, the share of total virtual gift consumption attributable to AI-generated interactive virtual gifts increased further to 35.4%.

Furthermore, Bigo Live continued to deepen local community engagement and foster vibrant creator ecosystems. In the Middle East and North Africa, as an official content partner of the 2026 Esports World Cup, Bigo Live delivered an immersive viewing format that integrated tournament livestreams with interactive experiences. Across Southeast Asia, Bigo Live hosted multiple mid-year galas in local markets, supporting the growth of local creators and the sustainable development of its ecosystem. In North America, BIGO Academy combined online growth challenges with offline recognition, highlighting the vitality of its creator ecosystem and strong user engagement. In South America, Bigo Live held its inaugural offline event in Brazil and organized roadshows in Colombia and Peru, expanding public awareness of the platform and fostering a more vibrant and inclusive local creator ecosystem.

BIGO Ads Advertising Technology Business

In the third quarter, BIGO Ads continued to expand its global traffic network, diversify its advertiser verticals and demand mix, while improving its algorithms and ad delivery efficiency. As a result, BIGO Ads' revenue reached US$145.7 million, up 39.6% year over year and 9.0% quarter over quarter. Its third-party advertising business, BIGO Audience Network, grew 52.3% year over year and 9.2% quarter over quarter.

On the supply side, BIGO Ads continued to expand its global developer ecosystem and broaden the high-quality traffic coverage. In the third quarter, SDK traffic grew 55.6% year over year. In October, BIGO Ads SDK became generally available via Google AdMob™ Mediation as an in-app bidding partner. Developers can now seamlessly access the BIGO Ads SDK through Google AdMob Mediation and tap into massive demand from global premium advertisers. This integration creates new opportunities for BIGO Ads to expand its premium traffic supply and reach a broader range of app categories.

On the demand side, BIGO Ads continued to strengthen its presence in key verticals by expanding its local advertiser base and accumulating more advertiser conversion data. These insights helped further refine its algorithms and optimize ad delivery solutions across different web-based verticals. Web-based advertising demand continued to accelerate, growing by approximately 328% year over year and 30% quarter over quarter, becoming a key driver of BIGO Ads' growth this quarter. Meanwhile, in-app demand maintained healthy growth momentum.

On the technology side, BIGO Ads continued to enhance its data and AI-driven algorithm capabilities to improve the precision and efficiency of ad delivery. As its cross-channel attribution systems improved and advertiser conversion data accumulated, the platform further upgraded its model architecture to support multiple conversion objectives and types of traffic, improving algorithm accuracy and iteration efficiency. Meanwhile, BIGO Ads continued to refine its bidding strategies to better assess the value of each ad impression and match advertiser budgets with available inventory more effectively. These improvements helped advertisers meet their ROI targets while enhancing the efficiency of BIGO Ads' traffic acquisition and monetization.

SHOPLINE E-Commerce Business

In the third quarter, SHOPLINE continued to focus on acquiring high-quality brand merchants, strengthening its presence in key markets, and enhancing its omnichannel commerce infrastructure and value-added services. SHOPLINE's revenue reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year and 10.0% quarter over quarter.

In the cross-border business, SHOPLINE enhanced its service offerings and local support to help these merchants migrate to its platform, manage operations across markets, and process cross-border transactions more efficiently. In the third quarter, revenue from cross-border merchants maintained strong momentum, growing 77.8% year over year. To support the growing base of brand merchants, the Company continued to enhance SHOPLINE Payments with more local payment options, stronger multi-currency payment support, and improved transaction management. These enhancements helped merchants manage cross-border payments easily and efficiently.

In AI Commerce, SHOPLINE's strategy revolves around helping merchants capture demand from AI channels and improve their operational efficiency. As AI agents change how consumers discover and purchase products, SHOPLINE continued to strengthen its capabilities and expand integrations with the broader AI ecosystem. While volume from AI channels is still in an early stage, adoption is building quickly. In the third quarter, page views and order volume from AI channels grew nearly 500% and 550% year over year, respectively. Notably, AI is demonstrating distinct advantages in categories such as consumer electronics and furniture, where shoppers weigh multiple options before buying. In these categories, AI can better interpret consumer needs, recommend relevant products, and guide shoppers toward a purchase. SHOPLINE Omi, an AI-powered commerce assistant, has rolled out features spanning product management, customer segmentation, promotional events, guidance on platform features and settings, and detailed store performance analysis, bringing AI deeper into merchants' day-to-day workflows and improving operational efficiency.

Key Terms

floating-ratefinancial
A floating-rate is an interest rate on a loan, bond or other debt that moves up or down over time based on a regularly published reference number, so the payments change as market rates change. For investors, that means income and interest costs track current market conditions—like a thermostat that adjusts with room temperature—offering protection when rates rise but adding uncertainty about future cash flow.
interest-onlyfinancial
A loan or payment plan where the borrower pays only the interest for a set period while the original loan amount (the principal) stays unchanged; after that period payments typically rise to cover principal or a lump-sum principal payment is due. For investors this matters because interest-only structures change cash flows and risk: they can boost short-term income but increase the chance of payment shock or default later, similar to renting a car without paying down the purchase cost until the final bill arrives.
bridge loanfinancial
A bridge loan is a short-term loan used to quickly provide funds until a larger, long-term financing option is in place. It acts like a temporary bridge, helping individuals or businesses cover immediate expenses or complete transactions without delay. For investors, it’s important because it offers quick access to cash but often comes with higher costs and short repayment periods.
